cues.en: Netflix has also published how they're producing recommendations, so let's dive into that next.
cues.zh: Netflix 也公布了如何產生推薦，接著深入看看。

cues.en: They're not quite as open as Google is, so the details of how their algorithms work aren't available unless you work there.
cues.zh: 他們不像 Google 那麼開放，所以除非在那裡工作，否則無法得知演算法運作的細節。

cues.en: But, they have shared a lot of higher-level lessons they have learned and the general approach they take.
cues.zh: 但他們分享了很多較高階的經驗，以及採用的一般方法。

cues.en: Our main source for this section comes from the book Recommender Systems Handbook, specifically chapter 11 which is called Recommender Systems in Inudstry: A Netflix Case Study.
cues.zh: 這一節的主要來源，是 Recommender Systems Handbook 這本書，具體來說是第 11 章，標題為 Recommender Systems in Industry: A Netflix Case Study。

cues.en: This paper dates from 2015, so I'm sure their approaches have evolved since then, perhaps to include deep learning, but we don't know for sure.
cues.zh: 這篇文章來自 2015 年，所以我相信方法之後已有演進，也許加入深度學習，但我們無法確定。

cues.en: More recently, they have also presented at industry conferences such as ACM's RecSys conference but the actual papers published are very high level in nature.
cues.zh: 最近，他們也在 ACM RecSys 等業界會議發表，但實際公開的論文，內容仍非常高階。

cues.en: Unlike YouTube, Netflix has no mandate, at least at the time of their writing, to use deep learning for every machine problem they encounter.
cues.zh: 與 YouTube 不同，至少在撰寫文章時，Netflix 沒有要求每個機器學習問題都使用深度學習。

cues.en: Instead, they bank on a hybrid approach that combines together the results from many different algorithms.
cues.zh: 他們採用混合方式，結合許多不同演算法的結果。

cues.en: The ones they've said they used in the past include RBM and SVD++, which they learned were worthwhile from the Netflix Prize.
cues.zh: 他們曾說過去用過的演算法，包括 RBM 與 SVD++，這是從 Netflix Prize 得知值得採用的方法。

cues.en: They've also said that they combine nearest-neighbor approaches with matrix factorization approaches to try and get the best of both worlds.
cues.zh: 他們也說，會把最近鄰方法與矩陣分解方法結合，嘗試兼取兩者優點。

cues.en: That's all they've said definitively, although they sort of give us a wink and a nod when they present an incomplete list of methods that are useful to know in their paper.
cues.zh: 這是他們唯一明確說出的內容，不過論文列出一些值得了解的方法，雖然清單不完整，卻有點像在暗示我們。

cues.en: This list includes linear regression, logistic regression, elastic nets, SVD, matrix factorization, RBM's, Markov Chains,
cues.zh: 清單包括線性迴歸、邏輯斯迴歸、彈性網路、SVD、矩陣分解、RBM、馬可夫鏈，

cues.en: Latent Dirichlet Allocation, Association Rules, Factorization Machines, Random Forests, Gradient Boosted Decision Trees, k-means,
cues.zh: 潛在狄利克雷配置、關聯規則、分解機、隨機森林、梯度提升決策樹、k-means，

cues.en: Affinity Propagation, and Dirichlet Processes.
cues.zh: 親和傳播，以及狄利克雷程序。

cues.en: I think this is Netflix's way of saying they basically try every algorithm out there, and let them all fight it out amongst each other when faced with the problem of generating recommendations for a given user.
cues.zh: 我想，這是 Netflix 在表示，他們基本上嘗試所有演算法，面對為某位使用者產生推薦的問題時，就讓這些演算法互相競爭。

cues.en: It's probably safe to say they're dabbling in deep learning by now as well.
cues.zh: 大概也可以合理推測，他們現在也開始涉足深度學習。

cues.en: So while Netflix seems intent on keeping the details of its candidate generation as a trade secret, they do share some higher level learnings, and details on their ranking approach.
cues.zh: 所以，Netflix 似乎打算把候選項目產生的細節保留為商業機密，但確實分享了高階經驗，以及排序方法的細節。

cues.en: One phrase that Netflix uses repeatedly in their publications is everything is a recommendation.
cues.zh: Netflix 的出版內容中，反覆出現一句話：「一切都是推薦」。

cues.en: The Netflix home page is organized into many rows, each row containing its own top-N list of recommendations for a given type of recommendation.
cues.zh: Netflix 首頁由許多列組成，每一列都針對某種推薦類型，包含自己的 Top-N 推薦清單。

cues.en: For example, my home page includes top picks, which presumably are my actual top-N results for me personally.
cues.zh: 例如，我的首頁有「精選推薦」，推測就是為我個人產生的實際 Top-N 結果。

cues.en: Continue watching is recommendations based on videos I've already watched or at least, the people in my family who share my account.
cues.zh: 「繼續觀賞」則根據我看過的影片推薦，或者至少是與我共用帳號的家人看過的影片。

cues.en: I also see a list of recommendations restricted to the genre I seem to be most interested in, which is TV sci-fi and fantasy.
cues.zh: 也會看到限制在我似乎最感興趣類型中的推薦，也就是科幻與奇幻影集。

cues.en: If I scroll down, there are countless more rows associated with recommendations for other categories I may be interested in, recommendations for new releases, for popular items, and for Netflix original series.
cues.zh: 往下捲動，還有無數列，與可能感興趣的其他類別、新上架、熱門項目，以及 Netflix 原創影集的推薦有關。

cues.en: Basically, everything is a recommendation their homepage is just a series of recommender engines tuned for some specific purpose.
cues.zh: 基本上，一切都是推薦。首頁就是一系列為特定目的調整過的推薦引擎。

cues.en: Netflix has gone all-in with relying on recommender engines to introduce their members to new content.
cues.zh: Netflix 全面依賴推薦引擎，向會員介紹新內容。

cues.en: Having all of these different recommenders on one page introduces its own set of challenges.
cues.zh: 把這麼多不同推薦器放在同一頁，也帶來一組挑戰。

cues.en: How do you make sure you don't repeat the same recommendation on the same page?
cues.zh: 如何確保同一頁不會重複出現相同推薦？

cues.en: How do you choose the best order to present these different recommendations in?
cues.zh: 如何選擇呈現不同推薦的最佳順序？

cues.en: This means that Netflix not only has to personalize movie and TV recommendations to you, they also have to personalize the order in which these recommendations are presented to you.
cues.zh: 這表示 Netflix 不只要為你個人化電影與電視節目推薦，也要個人化這些推薦呈現的順序。

cues.en: This is called whole-page optimization, and using machine learning to optimize the selection of individual rating widgets on slots on a page is a technique that can be
cues.zh: 這叫做整頁最佳化。使用機器學習，最佳化頁面不同位置要選擇的個別推薦元件，是一種，

cues.en: powerful for any website.
cues.zh: 對任何網站都可能很有力的技術。

cues.en: If you look at Amazon.com's home page, it has a similar structure, and they face the same problem of page optimization to put the right features in the right slots on that page for you.
cues.zh: 看看 Amazon.com 首頁，也有類似結構，面臨相同的頁面最佳化問題：為你把合適功能放在頁面的合適位置。
